items: -ish, -ic, -al, -ed; having a particular quality of, pertaining to, associated with; forms adjectives from nouns, and sometimes from verbs — культу́ра (“culture”) + -ный → культу́рный (“cultural”); ме́сто (“place”) + -ный → ме́стный (“local”); наро́д (“people”) + -ный → наро́дный (“folk”)

blocks.text: A velar (as well as ц) normally turns into a palatal as a result of the Slavic first palatalization. This and the following several properties are due to the *ь that was formerly present at the beginning of the suffix.

items: -ish, -ic, -al, -ed; having a particular quality of, pertaining to, associated with — дверь (“door”) + -ной → дверно́й (“door”); за́пись (“notation, (plural) notes”) + -ной → записно́й (“intended for notes”)

Used to form adjectives from nouns or sometimes other adjectives, often relational (meaning "related to X"): -ian, -ic, -ish — А́нглия (“England”) + -ский → англи́йский (“English”); Русь (“Rus”) + -ский → ру́сский (“Russian”); ара́б (“Arab”) + -ский → ара́бский (“Arabic, Arabian, Arab”)

blocks.text: Historically triggered the first Slavic palatalisation, cf. гре́цкий, оне́жский, че́шский. However, in the modern literary language it has been replaced by the Church Slavonic variant -еский in most old formations. In modern formations, -ский after unmodified velars is used; e. g. ба́скский, стра́сбургский, каза́хский.
Always triggers palatalisation for stems in -л.

Historically pronounced as an unstressed -ской and sometimes also spelled as such. In early modern poetry, such as in Pushkin, rhyming of -ский with -ой can be found. This pronunciation became obsolete during the 20th century.

items: Used to form adjectives from nouns, often relational (meaning "related to X"): -ian, -ic, -ish — склад (“warehouse”) + -ской → складско́й (“warehouse (relational)”); заво́д (“factory”) + -ской → заводско́й (“factory (relational)”); муж (“man”) + -ской → мужско́й (“male, masculine, man's”)

blocks.text: Pairs from Wiktionary's etymologies: each right-hand word is the left-hand word + -ный / -ной / -ский / -ской, as Wiktionary records it.
